Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Contents 2 Setup 3 Play 4 Winning Contents The deck consists of 36 cards, numbered 1-12 three times. Setup Deal 9/8/6/6 cards (with 3/4/5/6 players) face down to the table. Players are dealt 9/7/6/5 cards, and their hands are arranged in numerical order. Play On your turn, take either of these actions up to three times: - Flip a table card face-up - Reveal a hand card : Choose any player (including yourself) and select a card at either end (Highest or Lowest number) of their hand: that card is placed face-up in front of them. If you reveal three cards with the same value, that's a success: claim this "trio" of cards as a scoring set. If you reveal a card that doesn't match those previously revealed that turn, you fail and your turn immediately ends. The revealed cards are returned to their previous position and state. Winning Simple mode : Win if you take three trios, or the trio of three 7s. Spicy mode : Win if you take two "connected" trios (where the cards of one trio include a small icon of the other), or the trio of three 7s. Note: A pair of numbers is connected if they differ by 7 (such as 3 and 10) or add up to 7 (such as 2 and 5). [Rating: 2/10] It's a very bad game with nothing inside. If you want a game to play with kids, try twin it.

[Rating: 2/10] It's me, not you. I just HATE memory games. I probably shouldn't be rating this, but it is what it is, I have to reflect how I feel about it.

[Rating: 3/10] I really dislike games with memory elements, and this one requires a good bit of it. However, there's a dose of luck that can allow non-memory players to potentially still win.  I love the art (in the original Nana edition), and think it's a great product! It's just not for me. I can see this being a very popular mass-market card game in the right hands.

[Rating: 3/10] A game of guessing, memory and very simple deduction. The idea is to reveal three cards of the same number in a single turn, by asking your opponents to reveal their lowest or highest card, flipping cards on the table or revealing your own. Slightly reminiscent of "Scout" and just as bad.

[Rating: 3/10] I can't believe it but my GeekBuddies actually quite like this. How? There's barely a game here, it's just Memory restructured.

[Rating: 3/10] It works fine - memory games just aren't for me. I'm not good at them and don't really care to be better.

[Rating: 3/10] This is a memory game, which I don't like. It adds another mechanism for interacting with other players by allowing you to ask them to reveal a card. So if you boil it down this game is essentially "Memory" and "Go Fish" mashed together. Probably fun for kids, but I didn't like it.

[Rating: 3/10] Game ends in less than 5 min. Doesn't really feel like a game. Memory set making.

[Rating: 3/10] A simple memory game that has some very nice cards. You're just asking other players at the table (or yourself) what their lowest or highest card is. You can also, optionally, flip a central offer of cards that belong to no one. The idea is to flip three cards in a row with the same value (three 2s, for example).  As everyone will have a jumble of cards, it's up to you to divine what people have and what's in the central offer.
